aliases: Tunka Advanced Instrument for cosmic rays and Gamma Astronomy

facility_roles.quote: in the Tunka valley 50 km to the west from Lake Baikal (51.49 N, 103.04 E)

intervals.label: TAIGA construction
intervals.note: Start: "In 2012 in the frame of Russian-German joint research activities, the construction of two new detectors was started." (Kostunin et al., arXiv:1903.07460, Section 2).
intervals.quote: In 2022, we completed the deployment and commissioning of the TAIGA-1 hybrid complex

intervals.label: TAIGA operation
intervals.note: 2013 is the year the first TAIGA-type array, Tunka-HiSCORE (later TAIGA-HiSCORE), went into operation; the Tunka-133 array had been taking data since 2009. The first IACT was deployed in 2017 and the second in 2018. The most recent statement read (2022) describes TAIGA-1 as complete and in operation.
intervals.quote: was put into operation one year later, in 2013

quantity.quote: It consists of 120 TAIGA-HiSCORE wide-angle Cherenkov stations
three 4-m class Imaging Atmospheric Cherenkov Telescopes (IACT)
250 m2 of scintillation particle detectors of TunkaGrande

lineage.note: Tunka-133 is one of the setups of the facility later named TAIGA. Row on the lexicographically smaller id (experiment:taiga).
lineage.quote: the entire facility was later called TAIGA (Tunka Advanced Instrument for cosmic rays and Gamma Astronomy)

name: TAIGA
notes: No official TAIGA website is recorded: taiga-experiment.info returned HTTP 404 and the other candidate hosts did not resolve (checked 2026-10-26).

TAIGA is recorded as one experiment because the collaboration's own lecture treats Tunka-133, Tunka-Rex, Tunka-Grande, TAIGA-HiSCORE and TAIGA-IACT as setups of one facility; Tunka-133 additionally has its own record because it has its own long series of results.

physics_goals.quote: Our goal is to establish a novel hybrid direct air shower technique, sufficient to access the energy domain of the long-sought Pevatrons.
physics_goals.value: Establish a hybrid air-shower technique able to reach the energy domain of Galactic PeV accelerators ("Pevatrons").

summary.plain: TAIGA combines three kinds of detector in a Siberian valley: light stations, imaging telescopes and particle counters. Together they hunt for PeV gamma rays and measure cosmic rays from 100 TeV to several EeV.
summary.technical: Hybrid detector complex in the Tunka valley: 120 TAIGA-HiSCORE wide-angle Cherenkov stations, three 4 m class IACTs and 250 m2 of scintillators (Tunka-Grande, TAIGA-MUON), with Tunka-133 and the Tunka-Rex radio array; TAIGA-1 completed 2022. Detected the Crab Nebula at 8.5 sigma with the first IACT.
